They make the design.”', and two h3 intro statements; there is no h1, and the eight topic tiles (Framework ... Motion), which are the page's navigation, are plain links with no list or nav label.

findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships and 2.4.6 Headings and Labels: a lone quote mark announced as a heading and a missing h1 leave no usable outline.

findings.evidence: The intro statements are revealed by scroll: the sweep found the same sentence at 13%, 16% and 21% opacity in successive frames, and the 375 frame shows the text alone on a mostly blank screen. With no prefers-reduced-motion rule (sweep), the reveal and the animated logo run for everyone.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (AAA, advisory) and 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide; text that is unreadable until the user scrolls a set distance also risks 1.4.3.

findings.evidence: bodyText reads 'Dropbox Brand Studio 🤝 Daybreak Studio': the emoji between the two credit links is announced as 'handshake'.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.1.1 Non-text Content: a decorative glyph needs to be hidden or given a meaningful text equivalent.

strengths: Tile labels are real text, not baked into images; topic colours do not carry meaning on their own (each tile is named).
Tile title colours hold contrast against their own fills at large size (e.g. navy/light blue, lime/dark green, lavender/purple).
not_investigated: disputed: A11-001 contrast 1.76:1 on 'Imagery' sampled a white #ffffff background; the title sits on the maroon tile, where pink #ffafa5 is about 5:1. Likely the white gutter between tiles.
